name: Congenital Anomaly of Hepatic Vein

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Hepatic Vein Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of abnormal hepatic vein anatomy or absence on imaging studies (ultrasound, CT, MRI)
Presence of clinical signs consistent with hepatic venous outflow obstruction or altered hepatic circulation
Exclusion of acquired causes of hepatic vein abnormalities such as thrombosis or trauma
Laboratory findings suggestive of hepatic dysfunction or congestion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed congenital hepatic vein anomaly with clinical signs and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or hypoplastic hepatic vein on imaging
searchTerms: missing or small liver vein on scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congestive hepatomegaly due to impaired venous outflow
searchTerms: enlarged liver due to vein blockage

common.symptomName: Abdominal distension secondary to hepatic congestion
Elevated liver enzymes indicating hepatic dysfunction
Peripheral edema related to venous congestion
searchTerms: swelling in legs from vein problems
enlarged spleen from high portal pressure
big spleen due to portal hypertension
fluid in abdomen from portal hypertension

occasional.symptomName: Jaundice due to impaired hepatic clearance
Fatigue related to chronic liver dysfunction
Mild right upper quadrant abdominal pain
searchTerms: mild pain in right upper belly

rare.symptomName: Hepatic encephalopathy secondary to severe liver dysfunction
Variceal bleeding due to portal hypertension
searchTerms: bleeding from swollen veins in esophagus

rare.symptomName: Coagulopathy from impaired hepatic synthesis of clotting factors

laboratory: Increased bilirubin levels in some cases
imaging: Ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic hepatic veins
CT or MRI demonstrating abnormal hepatic venous anatomy and hepatic congestion
Doppler studies revealing altered hepatic venous flow
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Histopathology may show hepatic congestion and fibrosis in advanced cases

distinguishingFeatures: Acquired hepatic vein thrombosis rather than congenital absence
Typically presents in adulthood with acute symptoms
Cardiac anomalies causing secondary hepatic venous congestion

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe hepatic dysfunction
Signs of portal hypertension with variceal bleeding
